items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: So Simon and John Marara both went with the Tuxedo Band, and I wanted to get over there. So I left Maple Leaf Band and I joined the Tuxedo Band

ctx.x: That fellow, Dave Dupas, he was an insurance collector. And he used to worry me, worry me, but John, the Tuxedo Band, that's a great band, and John would... Well, Simon was playing with the Kid René Band, he quit the band and he went with the Tuxedo Band. So Simon and John Marara both went with the Tuxedo Band, and I wanted to get over there. So I left Maple Leaf Band and I joined the Tuxedo Band, that was in 1923. Who was the actual leader?
Celestan or Ridgely? No. Bebe Ridgely. That was the manager of the band.

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: So I took Simon Marrera, John Marrera, and myself and Abbie Foster, Chinese we called him, drum player. We went over to Celestad's house and talked Celestad into making up his own band.

ctx.x: But anyway, we thought probably Celestad wasn't getting a right deal, but maybe Ridgely may be in the right, we actually don't know. But before Ridgely died they told me it was just concerning a little money. And it was a terrible mistake that they made because the band was too great. So I took Simon Marrera, John Marrera, and myself and Abbie Foster, Chinese we called him, drum player. We went over to Celestad's house and talked Celestad into making up his own band. And called it Celestad's original Tuxedo band.…

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1969-06-16
items.q: Sometimes Buddy would send Louis Armstrong into his place, and John Marrero.

ctx.x: What bands did you hear Sidney work with? I mean, who was he playing with at this time, Sidney Bechet?

At the time before Sidney left, he was playing with a band, they called himself, the Young Olympia band. And that was with Siren Moreira, and Buddy P.T. Sometimes Buddy would send Louis Armstrong into his place, and John Marrero. They had a wonderful band. Yeah.

Did the, I mean music, when you were coming out, was it the same sort of thing as now? I mean the trumpet would just play a couple of choruses in the lead, and then they'd take solos? No, no, they didn't do that.
